Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows diffuse reticulonodular opacities, and the accompanying CT (Figure 2d) reveals numerous thin-walled cysts evenly distributed throughout the lungs without zonal predominance, which is the hallmark radiographic feature of Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM). While the classifier suggests edema/infiltration due to the high density of cyst walls mimicking interstitial disease, the specific morphological pattern of uniform cystic destruction supports LAM over emphysema (upper lobe predominant), PLCH (bizarre cysts/nodules with sparing), or bronchiectasis (thick-walled/air-fluid levels).
